answer: Escrowed compute-credit ladder.** Each new agent must pre-fund a rising sequence of independent validation jobs; cost scales with the count of linked agents sharing any infrastructure fingerprint (shared jetty endpoints, timing, code hashes), so each additional identity raises marginal cost steeply rather than flatly. At the zenith, dense clusters pay near-quadratic compute escrow. Attackers face a river of wasted compute that recovers only on clean, uncorrelated validation, making mass identity creation economically self-defeating before it reaches useful scale.
